A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Low-Rank Thinning by the same authors. Their complete main texts and appendices A–L are readable, and corresponding equations, algorithms, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original attention-approximation results on ImageNet, SGD convergence experiments on mortgage data, and deep-kernel testing experiments on Higgs data in Table 3 and Figures 1–2.

after.justification: v5 retains these three original empirical studies, including revised attention and Higgs testing results.

M1.justification: Thinformer, thinned SGD reordering, CTT, and the appendix thinning algorithms retain their procedures and components. The changed attention compression parameter is an experimental configuration change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet classification with T2T-ViT attention replacements, mortgage logistic regression, and Higgs two-sample testing. No dataset, task, population, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: exact attention, Performer, Reformer, KDEformer, and ScatterBrain for attention; RR and both CD-GraB variants for SGD; and W-Block and Subsampling for CTT.

E3.justification: Table L.1 changes Thinformer's second-layer compression setting from g=3 to g=4. Appendices L.1 and L.3 revise the hardware/software environments, including A6000 to A100 for attention and different H100 configurations for testing. The datasets, metrics, sample sizes, and timing procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing compression-versus-power analysis in Figure 2 is revised: CTT power at g=3 and g=4 changes from approximately 0.80/0.95 to 0.63/0.85. This updates the evidence about the compression trade-off while retaining the same sweep; no additional ablation or robustness study appears.

E5.justification: Reporting practices remain unchanged: Table 3 uses standard deviations over five accuracy seeds and 50 timing batches, Figure 1 uses five seeds, and Figure 2 uses standard errors over 1000 trials with 100 permutations. Updated uncertainty values do not introduce a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Two central empirical result sets are substantially revised. In Table 3, Thinformer's layer runtimes change from 3.72/0.81 ms to 2.06/0.54 ms, overtaking Performer on both layers; its accuracy changes from 82.17±0.04% to 82.18±0.05%, alongside comparator updates. Figure 2 replaces the time-power curves, with upper power values around 0.85 instead of 0.96. Different reported platforms and configurations limit direct cross-version performance comparisons.

T1.justification: Localized mathematical revisions preserve the principal rates. Appendix C.1.2 corrects the squared probability-vector norm to use input size nin rather than ambient n. Lemma G.2 aligns its rank threshold with Theorem 3 and changes the additive term under the square root from 4 to 1. Theorem 4 changes log(n/s) to log((m+n)/s), and Appendix I replaces an asserted equality with an asymptotic bound. The alternative covering-number rate is also restated using Theta rather than O.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding Impact Statement retain the same central contributions: general low-rank thinning guarantees and applications to attention, SGD reordering, and near-linear two-sample testing.

C2.justification: The discussion after Corollary 4 explicitly contrasts eigenvalue and covering-number analyses and states that the alternative lacks known intrinsic-manifold adaptivity. Section 6.2 also qualifies the empirical dominance description by removing 'uniformly'.

D1.justification: Appendix L adds SGD learning rate 0.01, loading batches of 16, and individual-datapoint gradient reordering. It also specifies deep-kernel training rate 5×10^-5 and full-training-sample batches. These expand previously referenced procedures without establishing that those settings changed. Hardware/software specifications are updated; code access information is retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is unchanged, but the comparison with Dwivedi and Mackey (2022) expands from worse dimension dependence to an explicit contrast between covering-number and eigenvalue approaches, including the absence of known intrinsic-dimension adaptivity for the alternative.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: the former Remark 1 becomes an expanded paragraph after Corollary 4, experimental and proof prose receives limited revisions, and acknowledgments are added. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with changed markers, annotations, legend typography, and x-axis ticks. Table 3 removes its dagger/star header markers and receives small formatting adjustments. Other changes are limited text reflow; no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The corrected input-size calculation, more consistent rank specification, and corrected asymptotic relationship improve mathematical precision. Appendix L's explicit learning rates and batching details also improve reproducibility. These are useful, localized gains. The refreshed benchmark results use changed platforms/settings, so their lower runtimes do not independently establish improved paper quality or a methodological advance.
